## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Tatiyapīṭhavimānavatthu* ("Third Throne Mansion", Vv 3) is a canonical verse narrative located in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Like many other narratives in this cycle, the text centers on the mechanics of karmic retribution and celestial reward, illustrating how even offering a simple object—such as a seat or bench (chair/throne)—to the Sangha can generate extraordinary spiritual and heavenly results [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].
The text shares extensive formulaic and thematic phraseology with other early Buddhist poetic narratives. According to machine text-reuse analysis, it shares 196 matching passages with 28 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest Pali match occurs with its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which incorporates large portions of the root verses (69 matches, with segments §4.2–7.4 corresponding to commentary sections §177–187 with 0.93 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. Within the canonical collection, it shares near-identical verse sequences with the other texts of the *Pīṭhavagga*, particularly *Catutthapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 4, sharing §0.1–8.4 with 0.97 similarity), *Dutiyapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 2), and *Paṭhamapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 1), as well as thematic overlap with *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10) and multiple other Vimāna narratives [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus detects an automated textual alignment with a Tibetan canonical text (BO_K01_D0007B-2_H0008-2, best score 45), though no curated external parallels are established [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
